name: Question 34
problem: Consider the arc of the curve $x=\frac{{y}^{3}}{12}+\frac{1}{y}$ that lies between the lines $y=1$ and $y=e.$ Calculate the surface area generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi y\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since we're given a curve in the form $x=f(y),$ we have 

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{y}_{1}}^{{y}_{2}}y\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${y}_{1}=1$ to ${y}_{2}=e.$ 

Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{{y}^{3}}{12}+\frac{1}{y})=\frac{{y}^{4}-4}{4{y}^{2}}\,⇒\,{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}=\frac{{y}^{8}-8{y}^{4}+16}{16{y}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{y}_{1}}^{{y}_{2}}y\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{e}y\sqrt{1+\frac{{y}^{8}-8{y}^{4}+16}{16{y}^{4}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{e}y\sqrt{\frac{{y}^{8}+8{y}^{4}+16}{16{y}^{4}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{e}\,y\sqrt{\frac{({y}^{4}+4)^{2}}{16{y}^{4}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{e}y(\frac{{y}^{4}+4}{4{y}^{2}})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{y}^{4}+4}{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}({y}^{3}+\frac{4}{y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}{(\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}+4\operatorname{ln}⁡y)\,|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}(\frac{{e}^{4}}{4}+4-\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{8}({e}^{4}+15).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 34
?

Consider the arc of the curve x=y312+1y that lies between the lines y=1 and y=e. Calculate the surface area generated when this arc is rotated 2π radians about the x-axis.

a
 π8(e4+15)
b
 πe24
c
 π15(e4+1)
d
 4π15(e4−12)
e
 πe432
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated 2π radians about the x-axis using the formula

S=∫2πyds.

Since we're given a curve in the form x=f(y), we have

ds=1+(dxdy)2dy. Therefore, we will use

S=2π∫y1y2y1+(dxdy)2dy.

We are told that the limits of integration are from y1=1 to y2=e.

Computing the derivative, we get

dxdy=ddy(y312+1y)=y4−44y2⇒(dxdy)2=y8−8y4+1616y4.

Therefore,

S=2π∫y1y2y1+(dxdy)2dy=2π∫1ey1+y8−8y4+1616y4dy=2π∫1eyy8+8y4+1616y4dy=2π∫1ey(y4+4)216y4dy=2π∫1ey(y4+44y2)dy=π2∫1ey4+4ydy=π2∫1e(y3+4y)dy=π2(y44+4ln⁡y)|1e=π2(e44+4−14)=π8(e4+15).
